title: NASA Opens Applications for Its Next Astronaut Class — Moon-Bound, Deadline Dec. 3
excerpt: Want to fly to the Moon? NASA is accepting applications for a new class of astronauts, the agency announced Saturday, Nov. 7, during an air show at Kennedy Spac
content:
Want to fly to the Moon? NASA is accepting applications for a new class of astronauts, the agency announced Saturday, Nov. 7, during an air show at Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

U.S. citizens have until 11:59 p.m. EST on Thursday, Dec. 3, to submit their completed application materials. NASA expects to make its final selection in late 2027, with the new candidates beginning training in early 2028.

This will be NASA's 25th astronaut class since the original Mercury Seven were announced in 1959. The new astronauts will join the agency as America returns to the Moon, builds a Moon base, and lays the groundwork for the first crewed missions to Mars, according to NASA's announcement, release 26-093.

Who can apply

Applicants must be U.S. citizens and hold a master's degree in a science, technology, engineering or mathematics field — engineering, biological science, physical science or computer science — from an accredited institution. They also need at least three years of related professional experience after completing the qualifying degree.

NASA's selection FAQ is explicit that neither military service nor flying experience is necessary. Test pilot school and medical residency must be finished by July 2027 for those paths to count toward the requirements.

Why now

NASA has 32 active astronauts, and the workload is outrunning the roster. Artemis III commander Randy Bresnik told the Associated Press on Saturday that the current workload far exceeds the number of available crew members. The agency last opened applications in 2024, when it says it received more than 8,000 applications; 10 candidates made the final cut in September 2025.

The new class is framed around the Moon rather than only low Earth orbit. NASA describes the recruits as supporting Artemis and future exploration — but selection is not a guarantee of a particular mission or destination. The agency has not announced the size of the new class; it reveals that number only at selection.

The selection timetable runs from the Nov. 7 vacancy announcement through application review from December to April 2027, with initial interviews and assessments at Johnson Space Center in Houston planned for spring. NASA calls that schedule tentative and says it may extend or accelerate it depending on how many applications arrive.

For students in Laredo and Webb County — including the engineering and science students at TAMIU and Laredo College — the window is short: about four weeks from announcement to deadline. The application and full details are on NASA's astronaut recruitment page.
